title: Add a security filter to a GPO
description: Add a group or user to the security filtering of a GPO.

parameters.name: targetName
parameters.label: User or group
parameters.description: Name of the user or group

examples.description: Simulate the action without running it (dry run). The -WhatIf switch shows what would change without applying anything. ESSENTIAL before any bulk action or critical change. Remove -WhatIf once checked to run it.
Run the action without an interactive confirmation. -Confirm:$false removes the prompts. Useful in automated scripts but use it with care: there is no safety net.
Make the command return the changed or created object in the pipeline. By default, Set- and New- cmdlets return nothing. -PassThru turns the output on for chained operations or immediate checks.

Show detailed information about the run of the command. -Verbose turns on debug messages to understand exactly what happens. Essential for troubleshooting and for understanding the internal operations.

notes: Security filtering limits the GPO to the given groups or users. Read is also required.

fr.title: Ajouter un filtre de sécurité à une GPO
fr.description: Ajoute un groupe ou utilisateur au filtrage de sécurité d'une GPO.
fr.notes: Le filtrage de sécurité limite l'application de la GPO aux groupes/utilisateurs spécifiés. Nécessite aussi Read.

targetName.label: Utilisateur/Groupe
